name: DeepSeek-V2: A Strong, Economical, and Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Language Model
problem: DeepSeekMoE proved MoE FLOPs scale, but the KV cache still grew with context, so long-context serving of a 236B MoE model was bound by cache memory rather than by the experts.
mechanism: Combines two independent mechanisms. (1) DeepSeekMoE: fine-grained mN experts with mK activated plus K_s always-on shared experts; 236B total, 21B activated per token, 128K context. (2) Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA): instead of caching K and V per KV head, project the hidden state once per token down to a low-dimensional latent, cache ONLY that latent, then up-project to per-head K and V at attention time, with decoupled RoPE applied to a separate small vector so positional information survives the down-projection. Per-token KV cache becomes O(d_c) instead of O(L * d_h * d_k) and, crucially, INDEPENDENT of the number of KV heads, so raising head count for quality no longer multiplies cache size. MLA is the mechanism that changes the serving memory bottleneck; the MoE block alone does not.
speedup_reported: Saves 42.5 percent of training cost relative to DeepSeek 67B while substantially improving quality (21B versus 67B active parameters). The inference-side MLA claim is reported as a KV-cache size reduction rather than a tokens/second number, so there is no serving throughput figure to quote. Reported on H800 GPUs, a China-market SKU close to H100 SXM compute.
